newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia recovery lifts fairly traded Helsinki.
newsitem.headline: Nokia recovery lifts fairly traded Helsinki.

text.p: Shares advanced on Thursday in fair trade led by a partial recovery in bourse-engine Nokia, with early calm giving way to steady dealing despite Wall Street's Thanksgiving holiday, brokers said.
The HEX index rose 0.54 percent to 2,382.67. Volume was 316 million markka.
Nokia closed 4.00 markka higher at 257.00, after dropping 9.40 on Wednesday. The telecommunications share accounted for 44 percent of total bourse turnover.
During the session Nokia announced a one billion French franc order for GSM telecom infrastructure, but brokers said the recovery began already before the news.
"The reaction to the news was rather dull," one said.

Forestry shares were softer, with UPM-Kymmene falling 0.50 markka to 89.00 while Enso ended flat at 34.80. UPM was the second most traded share, with volume over 37 million markka -- some it in big inhouse deals, brokers said.
Brokers could not explain the divergent performance of Finnish and Swedish forestry shares, as Swedish forestries gained 4.6 percent in Stockholm on Thursday.
Bank share Merita added 0.10 markka to 14.50 in thin trade.

Metal shares were strong, with Metra rising 3.00 markka in active trade, and Valmet gaining 0.50 to 76.00 markka after it said it had sealed a deal to sell a tissue paper machine to Procter & Gamble of the U.S. for an undisclosed sum.
Brokers said there was brisk trade in small cap shares. "The over-the-counter list seems to be booming," one said.
"It looks like just about anything goes in small shares," said another.
Brokers said they expected the session's calm but positive trend to continue on Friday.
